shardRule: sha256(familyId) mod 3 over the full hex digest
sourceOfTruthForSourceBinaries: release rcap-d-source-packs-2026-08-12 (id 369314157); all three pack archives downloaded and their sha256 matched the release digests before use
method: Every finalized PDF and contact sheet was extracted from its lane branch at the manifest-recorded commit with `git cat-file blob` and opened with pdf-lib.
Every source binary was taken from the verified release packs, re-hashed, and opened.

What the factory WROTE was separated from what the SOURCE already carried by diffing each artifact's drawn text against a blank-flattened render of the same source binary, round-tripped through save/load so pdf-lib's flattened appearances are readable by D0's walker.

Value geometry was measured with the metrics of the font that actually draws each run; where D0's walker reports metricsExact:false (pdf-lib's standard Helvetica carries no /Widths) the width was recomputed from Helvetica metrics rather than the 500/1000 fallback.
Each drawn value was attributed to an exact field by matching the flattened widget XObject's placement and BBox to the census rectangle, not by guessing from overlapping rectangles.
A sample of artifacts was rasterised with pdftoppm and read as images.

crossCuttingFindings.title: Lane D1B records field withholdings but does not apply them to the render
crossCuttingFindings.detail: d1b-regenerate.mjs computes `bindings` and `bindingRefusals` (including 25 withheld_by_lane_review decisions across this shard's D1B families) and then calls finalizeOfficialForm with the UNFILTERED `census`. finalizeOfficialForm re-runs D0's decideBinding over every census entry, so the lane's withholdings never reach the renderer. D1A does the opposite and is the model: `const renderCensus = census.filter((f) => !laneRefusedNames.has(f.name))`. Affects 7 of the 15 D1B families in this shard, 32 field-level leaks across canonical and boundary fixtures. Map and artifact were written in the same commit, so this is not a stale-render problem.

crossCuttingFindings.title: D0 descriptor ordering binds the wrong fact on composite field names
crossCuttingFindings.detail: FACT_DESCRIPTORS is resolved first-match-wins, and its order does not match its specificity. participant.street_address (index 5) is listed above participant.city, participant.zip and participant.email, so EmailAddressOfRecord, ...MailingAddressCity and ...MailingAddressZip all bind the street address. participant.full_legal_name matches on a bare \bname\b, so BankNameAndAccountType and 'Street Number And Street Name' bind the participant's name. participant.city (\bcity\b) is listed above matter.county, so a Virginia 'CITY OR COUNTY' venue field binds the participant's home city. D1B documented every one of these in its withholding notes; because XC-1 discards the withholdings, they are visible in shipped artifacts. Independent of XC-1, NC:aoc-cv-226-support-en carries three of them as DECLARED bindings, so fixing XC-1 alone will not clear that family.

crossCuttingFindings.title: D0 factory cannot finalize a source carrying rich-text AcroForm fields
crossCuttingFindings.detail: Reproduced first hand on MO CR-145: form.updateFieldAppearances() raises pdf-lib RichTextFieldReadError and no artifact can be produced. One family in this shard; the lane's disclosure and no-fill handling were correct.

crossCuttingFindings.title: Evidence key names and types diverge across lanes in ways that would mislead an importer
detail: source-record.json non-filing key: `nonFilingNotice` present in D1A/D1B/D1C/D2A (null, or an OBJECT {notice,page,decodeBasis,cmapsConsulted,matched} in D1B); D3A instead uses `nonFilingNoticeOnFace`; D2B and D3B carry neither. The manifest flattens D1B's object to a STRING. An importer keying on source-record.nonFilingNotice sees nothing for D2B/D3A/D3B and would read 'no hold' on a form that carries one.

reports/protected-fields-scan.json `expectedValues` is an array in every lane except D3A, where it is a NUMBER (a count). Iterating it throws - it threw in this review's own tooling before being guarded.

field-census.json means different things per lane under the same keys: rcap-field-census/v3-first-hand and v4-lane-d1c count AcroForm terminal fields, while D3B's rcap-flat-slot-census/v1 counts measured flat rule-line blanks. Eight families in this shard report a non-zero `fieldCount` for a source with zero AcroForm fields.
reports/populated-fields.json is a bare array in D1A/D1B/D2A/D2B/D3A, but an object keyed canonicalWritten/boundaryWritten in D1C and count/fields in D3B.
The contact-sheet proof lives at contact-sheet/contact-sheet-proof.json in D1A/D1B/D1C/D2A/D3A and at reports/contact-sheet-proof.json in D2B/D3B.

productionHolds vocabulary is not a controlled list. The same concept appears as `track_level_import_mapping_required`, `legal_review_mapping_requires_track_level_import_mapping`, `legal_review_mapping:requires_track-level import mapping` and `legal_review_requires_track-level import mapping`; currentness appears as `source_currentness_gate_open`, `source_or_currentness_gate_open`, `freshness_source_or_currentness_gate_open` and `freshness:source_or_currentness_gate_open`. Some identifiers embed spaces and colons. A consumer keying on hold identity would treat these as distinct and could fail to block.
The manifest's `legalDesign` field carries seven distinct spellings across 94 families, including the bare value `unrecorded` for 31 of them.

crossCuttingFindings.title: The shared contact-sheet proof can be satisfied by pre-printed text
crossCuttingFindings.detail: missingExpectedValues strips whitespace and tests substring containment against the whole document, so a short expected value is 'proved visible' by any pre-printed occurrence. Six families in this shard pass the proof for a value that also appears on the blank panel: 'XX' (AL:sbi-form-46-support-en), 'OR' (IA:rule-2-86...), 'ND' (ND:expertise-form-instructions-en) and 'District Court' (VA:cc-1201-a, cc-1203-a, cc-1203-b). In all six the value is genuinely written as well - confirmed independently against a blank-flattened baseline - so no artifact is wrongly proved here, but the proof does not by itself establish that.

crossCuttingFindings.title: D0 text extraction cannot read Identity-H CID text, so text-derived proofs are blind on such sources
crossCuttingFindings.detail: extractTextItems does not consult a font's ToUnicode CMap, so CID-encoded documents return glyph codes. Confirmed on the four NC non-filing families and WA:blake-005-form-en. Bounded impact in this shard: factory-written values are drawn by pdf-lib in WinAnsi Helvetica and read back correctly, so no visibility proof is wrong; but any source-text-derived check (placeholder scanning, notice detection, anchor placement) is blind on these documents. D1B and D2A both worked around it independently - D1B by decoding ToUnicode itself for the non-filing scan, D2A by excluding CID lines from anchor placement - which is the right outcome reached twice in two different ways.

crossCuttingFindings.title: Claims checked that this shard could not reproduce
detail: ESM issue around the non-filing notice: NOT REPRODUCED. finalizeOfficialForm called with a nonFilingNotice against NC AOC-CR-287(VI) throws NonFilingHoldError, `err instanceof NonFilingHoldError` is true across the module boundary, and the notice survives on the error object.

UTF-8 issue in the shared verifier: NOT REPRODUCED as stated. scanBytesForActiveContent decodes with latin1 and redacts stream payloads before matching, which is correct; it returned inspectable:true with zero residue on all 116 artifacts opened. The real encoding limitation is in text extraction, recorded separately as XC-6.

WA anchor issues: CONFIRMED as accurately reported by lane D2A, and correctly handled - blake-005 has a CID-only text layer, crrlj-09-0200 and crrlj-09-0800 yield no matchable participant label, blake-003 measured labels but held the write box. No fill was produced in any of these cases and none was claimed.

TX GC-411 page access: PARTLY CONFIRMED. Only TX:tx-gc-411-073-instructions-instructions-en is unloadable, and the cause is the source binary itself, not page access in the factory. The other eight TX GC-411 families in this shard load and finalize normally.
CO JDF-683 overlay: NOT IN THIS SHARD. sha256('CO:jdf-683-...') does not land in shard 2, so this review makes no finding about it.
